title: Examples: streaming best practices + safe retry configuration (Python/TS/Go)
author: Sabrina James
description: Summary: Updates the example apps to reflect the cross-SDK streaming + retry standards work. Adds a new streaming-focused “chat streaming” example in TS/Node, and refreshes the existing Python + Go examples to demonstrate: (1) how to set timeouts for streaming vs non-streaming, (2) safe retry configuration (retry non-streaming requests on 429/5xx/transport errors; do not auto-retry mid-stream disconnects by default), (3) cancellation semantics (AbortController / context cancel) and deterministic cleanup, and (4) debugging hooks (log request-id, never log API keys). Motivation: We keep seeing customers copy/paste older snippets that either retry too aggressively on 429 (amplifying throttling) or treat streaming disconnects as “retryable” and end up duplicating partial outputs. This PR aligns examples with the SDK parity audit outcomes and reduces support load. Behavior: The examples default to the SDK defaults (no custom retry) but include an explicit “safe overrides” section showing how to tune max attempts, backoff, and timeout budgets. For streaming, we show how to surface disconnects with enough context (request-id, elapsed time, last event type) and recommend app-level resume logic only when the app has a dedupe/idempotency story. Notes: This PR intentionally avoids introducing any example that auto-retries streaming after partial tokens; we only demonstrate user-driven reconnect and UI affordances. Related: ENG-2483 (streaming semantics), ENG-2485 (conformance harness), ENG-2491 (docs updates). Also pairs with SDK PRs in progress (python: streaming hardening; ts: AbortController semantics; go: reader robustness).
commits: examples(streaming): add ts/node streaming chat example with cancellation + request-id logging
examples(retry): document safe retry tuning + budgets; avoid retrying mid-stream disconnects
examples(python): refresh streaming snippet; clarify timeout configuration and proxy buffering notes
examples(go): align context cancellation + streaming reader loop; add troubleshooting section
docs(examples): consolidate README guidance; add cross-language parity notes
review_conversation: Ibrahim Khan (review): Can we make the guidance crisper on what is retryable vs not? Customers will interpret any “reconnect” snippet as blessed retry semantics. Also please link the standard doc section once it lands. Sabrina James (author): Updated TS/Node README to explicitly say: “Do not auto-retry after receiving any streaming event/data.” Added a bold callout and moved reconnect to an “App-specific resume” section with a disclaimer about dedupe. Will add final link to the streaming ADR once published; for now referenced ENG-2483. Dana Lo (review): For Node, please ensure AbortController cancellation closes the stream reader and doesn’t leave the process hanging in examples. Also make sure we don’t instruct users to set overly low read timeouts for streaming. Sabrina James (author): Added a finally { reader.cancel() } and ensured response.body is closed. Updated timeout guidance: overall timeout is recommended; read timeout should be disabled or set high for SSE; added a note about proxies buffering (ties to SUP-9321). Mateusz Zielinski (review): Go example: retry loop should honor context cancellation immediately; right now it sleeps full backoff even after ctx.Done(). Sabrina James (author): Fixed backoff sleep to select on ctx.Done() and return promptly. Added a small unit test for the backoff helper. Rafael Mendes (review): Please add a note about 429 handling: respect Retry-After; cap retry attempts; add jitter; and explicitly warn against “infinite retries”. The previous examples implied “keep trying”. Sabrina James (author): Updated safe retry section: maxAttempts=3 by default, respects Retry-After when present, exponential backoff with jitter, and “retry budget” language. Removed “keep trying” phrasing. Wei Chen (review): README is long; can we add a quick “copy/paste minimal snippet” per language and move deep troubleshooting to shared doc? Sabrina James (author): Done. Added minimal snippets at top of each example README and moved proxy buffering / corporate MITM notes to examples/_shared/troubleshooting.md. Approvals: Ibrahim Khan approved after updates. Dana Lo approved. Mateusz Zielinski approved. Rafael Mendes approved with note to keep wording aligned to SRE guidance. Wei Chen approved.
release_notes: Examples repo only: Adds new TS/Node streaming chat example and updates Python/Go streaming examples to reflect SDK parity standards for streaming cancellation, timeouts, and safe retry configuration (no auto-retry mid-stream by default).
